reason: H0 fuzzes only raw plist deserialization followed by plist_free; it never exercises the PList::Integer copy constructor changed in S1. That constructor now frees its initially created _node and replaces it with plist_copy(i.GetPlist()), creating fuzz-worthy copy, ownership, and semantic-preservation behavior outside H0's coverage.
evidence: All four H0 targets call one of plist_from_bin, plist_from_json, plist_from_openstep, or plist_from_xml and then plist_free(root_node).
No H0 target constructs, copies, assigns, or destroys a PList::Integer object.
S1 changes PList::Integer::Integer(const PList::Integer&) from plist_set_uint_val(_node, i.GetValue()) to plist_free(_node) followed by _node = plist_copy(i.GetPlist()).
The changed constructor introduces an allocation/lifetime transition and copies the underlying plist object rather than only the uint64_t value.
recommended_action: Add a C++ API fuzz target that derives Integer instances from fuzz-controlled plist data and values, invokes the PList::Integer copy constructor, validates copied integer semantics and independence, and exercises destruction of both source and copy under sanitizers.
